narrative: Inventory optimization for PL1__MBCDAD62 reveals a moderate-variability demand regime (CV=0.47) with a statistically significant downward trend (slope=-29.42 units/day). Lead time is the dominant uncertainty driver at 73% of total variance, with a CV of 0.50 indicating highly volatile supplier performance. The recommended (r,Q) policy raises safety stock from 4,340 to 12,447 units to achieve a 95% service level, at a marginal annual cost increase of $281. Storage capacity remains well within limits at 27.7% utilisation.
warnings: Recommended policy increases costs by $281.13 annually due to higher safety stock
Lead time CV (0.50) is very high - consider supplier performance improvement
Significant demand trend detected (slope=-29.42) - review forecast model regularly

research_insights.selected_model: EOQ with stochastic lead time — continuous-review (r,Q) policy
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (98.4% non-zero), normally distributed, and at scale; EOQ minimises ordering/holding trade-off while the safety stock term absorbs combined demand and lead-time variance. Continuous review is appropriate given the high daily throughput and volatile lead times.
research_insights.boundary_risk: MODERATE — storage capacity is not binding (27.7% utilisation), but the large safety stock uplift (+187% vs SAP) should be validated against physical storage layout before implementation.
